title: Attributes the compiler and CLR actually honor
hook: Attributes attach metadata to assemblies, types, and members. Some are pure documentation; others change compiler behavior, serialization, validation, or run-time code paths — like [Required], [JsonPropertyName], or [Obsolete].

blocks.text: An attribute is a class deriving from System.Attribute applied in square brackets. The compiler stores attribute instances in metadata. Frameworks read them via reflection or source generators: ASP.NET Core reads [HttpGet], System.Text.Json reads [JsonIgnore], nullable reference types use [NotNullWhen]. Custom attributes can drive your own tooling if you read them at compile time or run time.

entries.plainDefinition: Metadata annotation on code elements, stored in assembly metadata.
Declares which targets a custom attribute can apply to.
Marks a member as deprecated; compiler can warn or error.

blocks.text: Auth tokens and API contracts often use attributes for validation ([Authorize], [Required], [MaxLength]). Serialization shape is attribute-driven in many stacks. Interviewers ask which attributes are compile-time versus run-time — [Conditional] is compile-time; [Serializable] is mostly legacy.

blocks.title: Compiler vs framework
blocks.body: The C# compiler understands a small set (Obsolete, Conditional, Nullable attributes). Most framework attributes are read by libraries at run time or by source generators at compile time.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Apply in source
items.body: [AttributeName] on target; constructor args become metadata.

items.title: Compiler embeds metadata
items.body: Attribute blobs stored in assembly tables.

items.title: Consumer reads metadata
items.body: Reflection, source generator, or framework scans at run/compile time.

items.title: Behavior changes
items.body: Validation runs, JSON name changes, route template binds.

snippet.label: Validation attributes on DTO
snippet.explanation: Model validation in ASP.NET Core reads these at run time before your handler runs.

snippet.label: JSON serialization attributes
snippet.explanation: System.Text.Json honors JsonPropertyName and JsonIgnore when serializing auth responses.

snippet.label: Custom attribute definition
snippet.explanation: Define reusable metadata. Your feature system reads it via reflection or a generator.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Attributes on properties that nothing reads — dead metadata. Wrong AttributeTargets so attribute does not compile on method. Assuming [Serializable] replaces proper DTO design in modern APIs.

interviewTakeaways: Attributes are metadata; frameworks read them via reflection or generators.
Compiler honors Obsolete, Conditional, nullable attributes directly.
Validation and JSON shape commonly use attributes on DTOs.
commonPitfalls: Custom attributes never read by any tool.
Attribute only on getter when validation expects property target.
Mixing Newtonsoft and System.Text.Json attribute sets.

jsTsCorrelations.note: TS decorators attach metadata similar to C# attributes but rely on emit helpers. C# stores attributes in CLR metadata tables.
